title: 3-bet wars
summary: Linear and polarized 3-bets, answering 3-bets in and out of position, and 4-bet bluffs.

why.text: In 6-max late opens are wide, so 3-bets are frequent, and 4-bets follow. To avoid becoming an easy target you have to 3-bet with some bluffs and also defend against 3-bets.

kinds.text:
Two kinds of 3-bet:
- **Linear** (merged): the best hands in a row, QQ+, AK, AQ, KQs, JJ–TT. Good against a player who calls 3-bets a lot.
- **Polarized**: strong hands plus bluffs like A5s, A4s, 76s, 65s; medium hands (AJo, KJs) call. Good in position against CO and button opens.

range.caption: Button against a CO open: a polarized 3-bet (pink) and calls (blue).

vs3bet.text:
Facing a 3-bet:
- **In position** call wider: pairs, suited broadways and aces, connectors; 4-bet QQ+, AK and a few bluffs.
- **Out of position** call tighter: a 3-bet pot without position is hard to play.
- The best **4-bet bluffs** are A5s–A4s: the ace blocks the opponent's AA and AK, and when called the hand still has equity.

q-4bet.q: Which hand suits a 4-bet bluff best?
q-4bet.explain: The ace blocks AA and AK; when called, A5s can still make a straight or a flush.

t2.q: Why is A5s a good 4-bet bluff?
options: The ace blocks the opponent’s AA and AK
t2.explain: Blocking the hands that continue makes the bluff work more often.

t3.q: Facing a 3-bet out of position, calls are usually…
t3.explain: Out of position you realize less equity in a bloated pot.
